The purchaser is likely to prevail because the easement was recorded and appurtenant to the woman’s house, so it passed with the property to the man and then to the purchaser, even though the man did not use it. The man’s temporary ownership of both parcels did not extinguish the easement because he never took actual possession of the house and there was no clear intent to merge the estates. Therefore, the purchaser holds a valid easement and the man cannot barricade the path.

CONFIDENCE: 90
